reason: Each normative SPEC.md FR-07 requirement maps to an assertion that fails when it is violated. v1 upgrade and downgrade: test_fr07.py:176 checks the tables exist at head, and :186 checks no tables remain after `downgrade base`. v2: :294-296 checks the offline SQL for `tags`, `task_tags` and the unique `tasks(name)` index, and :323 checks a duplicate name is rejected. v2 downgrade: :359-372 checks v1 rows, api_keys and result_json survive, the new tables are gone, and the unique name index is gone. v3 data migration and reverse migration: :216-220 checks task_results is dropped and result_json is back with all 3 rows populated, :223 checks result_json is removed after re-upgrade, and :231-233 and :403-405 compare every column's value and type for all rows, including adversarial NULL, unicode and large values. Round trip: :214 and :222 run `downgrade -1` then `upgrade head`, and :236 checks the tasks columns are unchanged. Upgrade and downgrade both succeed: :182-187. No DROP shortcut: :272 AST-scans the migration string constants for DROP TABLE. Offline SQL generation: :289-293. Revision chain and real downgrades: :155-162. One minor gap: the no-shortcut scan only looks at string constants. The data-loss assertions would still catch a destructive downgrade.
